raw_response:
I am 53 years old, been farming this 5 mu in Quzhou County for 33 years. I only went to primary school, but I know this land better than any book. My household has seven people—my wife, my son and daughter-in-law who work in the county town but come back for busy seasons, and my grandchildren. Money is always tight, so I don't take risks.

For the winter wheat, I plant in early October, same as everyone in the village. I use the improved variety from the seed station, about 15 kg per mu. Before planting, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu—that's what my father did, and what my neighbors do. I learned my lesson years ago: better a little too much fertilizer than too little. At Qingming, when the wheat starts jointing, I topdress with about half a bag of urea per mu if it looks yellow. I'll irrigate three times: at jointing, at heading, and once during grain filling if the weather stays dry. Pumping water costs money, but I've seen what drought does at heading—you lose everything. I spray herbicide once after planting, and insecticide if I see aphids.

For summer maize, the window is brutal. After wheat harvest in early June, I hire the combine so we can get maize in the ground by mid-June. No time for deep plowing—I just run the rotary tiller once and plant. I buy hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, and one more round of urea when the maize is knee-high. Two irrigations should be enough, maybe three if it's very hot in July. My family does most of the work, but I hire a few days of labor during harvest and planting when everyone is scrambling.

Last year I got about 400 kg per mu of wheat and 450 kg per mu of maize. If the weather is normal and prices don't crash, I hope for the same. I can't afford to gamble on new methods.
